cluster_summary: A cluster of vulnerabilities where user-controlled wiki content is executed with the wrong security context (e.g., viewer's or page author's privileges instead of content owner's) or where missing required-rights analyses allow low-privileged users to inject script content that later executes with elevated privileges.
guideline_text: Trace lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities into server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs. Report code paths where a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 13 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege.

mechanism.missing_guard: a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability
mechanism.name: privileged server-side capability exposed to lower privilege context
mechanism.sink_shape: server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs
mechanism.source_shape: lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities
mechanism.typical_fix: check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Explicitly pass the restricted flag to all derived contexts, or set it on documents.
sub_patterns.name: Missing propagation of restricted execution context flag
sub_patterns.root_cause: The security flag indicating restricted/sandboxed execution is not propagated to sub-contexts (transformation contexts, async jobs, field registrations, historical versions), causing content to be evaluated with default permissive privileges.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Register proper analyzers that declare required rights (e.g., WIKI_ADMIN, PROGRAM, SCRIPT) and add authorization gates before content evaluation.
sub_patterns.name: Missing required-rights analysis for editable objects with executable content
sub_patterns.root_cause: The platform lacks RequiredRightAnalyzer implementations for certain object types or property configurations, or authorization checks (e.g., script rights, VIEW rights) are missing before rendering user-provided scripting content.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Execute content with the correct user's rights (author, creator) or parse immediately in the correct context, and disable async/caching that could reuse privileged outputs.
sub_patterns.name: Content executed under wrong user's security context
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled content (macro parameters, footnotes, UI extensions, cached results) is rendered using the privileges of a different user (viewer, page author, or a high-privilege entity) instead of the content author or creator, allowing privilege escalation.
